pages.title: Learn
pages.summary: A lifelong student of systems, networking, voice, and the contact center, studying AI omni-channel agents. The map is prompt, model, retrieval, tools, and an eval gate.

pages.title: Diagrams
pages.summary: The room drawings are the 38 files from the study folder. The animated flows are ladders, routing, architecture, deployment, cutover, and a troubleshooting tree drawn for this course.

pages.title: Flows
pages.summary: 14 call, signal, and data flows. Each picture moves a packet along the study path. Emergency stays on the voice platform. Reduced motion hides the packet.

pages.title: Charts
pages.summary: Every bar is a count from the lesson files in this build. Nothing here is a vendor dashboard.

pages.title: Cheat Codes
pages.summary: 10 topic sheets, each as HTML, PDF, PNG, and SVG, plus a flashcard JSON of 400 cards and a printable flashcard PDF. The zip is the full offline campus.

pages.title: Play
pages.summary: Browser labs for prompts, retrieval, tools, and evals. No key is required to read them.

pages.title: Ecosystem
pages.summary: Map sister systems, ports, cutovers, and the claims this course will not certify.

pages.title: Licensing, certification, and a career path
pages.summary: This course issues no certificate. Vendor exams change. The portfolio that matters is a trace, a task set, and a written gate.

pages.title: How to use this campus
pages.summary: One file, a track order, and a way to know what you have finished.

pages.title: What you are learning to do
pages.summary: The skill is judgment you can show, not a tour of product names.

pages.title: Keep proof for every exercise
pages.summary: Run, trace, metric, and artifact: four fields that make a lesson repeatable.

pages.title: Safety rules for every exercise
pages.summary: Private data stays local until you have a reason to move it, and some actions always wait for a person.

pages.title: What you need on your machine
pages.summary: A current browser is enough to study. A local model is optional and comes later.

pages.title: How the tracks fit together
pages.summary: Models, then prompting, then a way to ground and act, then proof that it worked.

pages.title: A model predicts the next token
pages.summary: Fluency is the product of a probability model. It is not a source of record.

pages.title: Tokens are the unit of cost and context
pages.summary: A token is a chunk of text, not a word, and every limit you hit is counted in tokens.

pages.title: The context window is one shared budget
pages.summary: Instructions, retrieved text, the conversation, and the answer all spend the same token limit.

pages.title: Temperature is a sampling control
pages.summary: Lower settings repeat likely tokens. Higher settings take more risks. Neither setting checks facts.

pages.title: Hallucination is fluent text without evidence
pages.summary: Catch it with sources, tools, and tests. Do not catch it by asking the model if it is sure.

pages.title: System, user, and tool messages do different jobs
pages.summary: Put standing rules in the system message. Put the task in the user message. Put tool results in tool messages.

pages.title: Model families you will see in 2026 job posts
pages.summary: Hire and design for a role, then pin an id. A family name is not a version.

pages.title: Choose a reasoning model or a fast chat model
pages.summary: Spend extra compute when the task needs a plan. Do not spend it on extraction you can score cheaply.

pages.title: What a language model computes
pages.summary: A language model turns the tokens so far into a probability for every token that could come next. Everything a chat product shows you is that loop, plus a sampler, plus a contract about messages. This room builds that picture so later rooms on retrieval, tools, and voice have somewhere to attach.

pages.title: Transformers and attention, walked through
pages.summary: Attention is a weighted sum of value vectors. The weights come from scaled dots between a query and the keys. This room walks that formula with numbers, then says what a 2026 model card adds and what it still refuses to draw.

pages.title: Write the job, the input, and the done-check
pages.summary: A prompt is a job description. If you cannot tell whether the answer succeeded, the prompt is not finished.

pages.title: Lock the output shape
pages.summary: Ask for a structure, then validate it in code. Prose that looks like JSON is not JSON.

pages.title: Few-shot examples that do not leak
pages.summary: Examples teach the pattern. They are also data you might not have permission to send.

pages.title: Split a hard task into steps you can test
pages.summary: One prompt that plans, searches, calculates, and drafts is several jobs hiding in a paragraph.

pages.title: Critique the draft, then revise once
pages.summary: A second pass helps when the critique is a checklist, not a request to 'make it better'.

pages.title: Prompt injection is untrusted text that pretends to be an order
pages.summary: Documents, web pages, and tool descriptions can carry instructions. Your system does not have to obey them.

pages.title: Change one thing, then score it
pages.summary: A prompt edit without a before-and-after score is a new opinion.

pages.title: Prompting and instruction design
pages.summary: A prompt is a specification the model will only partly obey. This room treats it as versioned text with a hierarchy, a set of examples that teach shape rather than truth, a schema that checks shape rather than policy, and a boundary around untrusted text. The controls that matter live outside the paragraph.

pages.title: Structured outputs and tool calling
pages.summary: A schema makes a shape. A tool call makes a request. Neither one is permission. This room separates OpenAI’s structured-output fields, the function-calling loop the application still has to run, and Anthropic’s tool-name rule, and it refuses to paste one vendor’s JSON onto another.

pages.title: Injection at the prompt boundary
pages.summary: Untrusted text can sit inside a trusted instruction. The controls that matter live outside the prompt: the tool list, the host cap, and the person who can deny a call. This room draws that boundary with the pages this lab already fetched, and it keeps instruction priority from being mistaken for a fix.

pages.title: Run a model locally when the data should stay put
pages.summary: Local is a privacy and latency choice. It is not automatically the more accurate choice.

pages.title: Install a runner and call it on localhost
pages.summary: Ollama and llama.cpp are the usual local runners. The smoke check is a local HTTP call or a CLI completion.

pages.title: Pick a model size that fits in memory
pages.summary: If the weights do not fit, the runner will swap, crash, or refuse. Start smaller than your pride.

pages.title: Quantization trades precision for fit
pages.summary: The weights are stored with fewer bits. You measure whether your tasks still pass.

pages.title: Read the license before you ship a weight
pages.summary: Open weights are not one license. Some allow commercial use. Some restrict it. Some restrict use of the outputs for training.

pages.title: Keep a smoke test you can rerun
pages.summary: After a reboot, prove the runner is up before you debug the prompt.

pages.title: Keep weights, prompts, and private data apart
pages.summary: Different files, different backups, different permissions.

pages.title: Call an API without putting the key in the repo
pages.summary: The key lives in an environment or a secret store. The client reads it at runtime. Logs do not print it.

pages.title: Ask for structured output and check it
pages.summary: Schema mode is a feature of the API. Your parser is still the gate.

pages.title: Set timeouts, retries, and a rate-limit plan
pages.summary: A hung call is a product bug. A retry storm is a bill.

pages.title: Read the bill in tokens, cache, and batch
pages.summary: Cost is a property of the design. Input tokens, output tokens, and tool calls are the levers.

pages.title: Compare providers on the same ten tasks
pages.summary: Swap the client. Keep the fixture, the schema, and the scorecard.

pages.title: Log the call without logging the secret
pages.summary: Keep the model id, the latency, the token counts, and a hash or id of the prompt. Drop the key and the raw private text unless you have a place to store it.

pages.title: LLMOps in production
pages.summary: A production model call is a span, a bill, a latency hop, and a guardrail. This room pins the OpenTelemetry GenAI names this lab will use, treats cost and latency as worksheets instead of slogans, and keeps the enforcement of a cap in the host.

pages.title: Retrieve when the answer has to come from a source
pages.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation finds passages first, then asks the model to answer from those passages.

pages.title: Chunk documents so a citation can point at them
pages.summary: Split on structure. Keep a stable id. Do not hunt for a magic token count.

pages.title: Search with keywords and with embeddings
pages.summary: Embeddings find similar meaning. Keywords find the exact name. Hybrid search uses both.

pages.title: Rerank a short list before you prompt
pages.summary: Retrieve widely, then keep the few passages that actually answer.

pages.title: Cite a passage a person can open
pages.summary: A citation is an id and a span, not a confident tone.

pages.title: Failure modes to test before you tune the prompt
pages.summary: Wrong chunk, stale chunk, lost middle, and a corpus that never contained the fact.

pages.title: Measure retrieval before you measure the answer
pages.summary: Recall on the right chunk is a different number from whether the paragraph was helpful.

pages.title: RAG end to end
pages.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation, in the system you will actually ship, is a pipeline: chunk a corpus, embed it with one model, search, pack a few passages into the prompt, and require the language model to answer from those passages or abstain. The 2020 paper that named RAG is a related but stricter thing: a seq2seq model and a dense index trained so the generator is marginalized over retrieved documents. This room keeps those two meanings apart and walks the production path from document to cited answer.

pages.title: Vector databases and hybrid search
pages.summary: pgvector stores vectors in Postgres and can index them with HNSW or IVFFlat. BM25 is a lexical score, and Elasticsearch documents it as the default similarity. Reciprocal rank fusion combines ranked lists. This room keeps those three mechanisms in separate sentences so a design review cannot pretend one extension does all three.

pages.title: An agent is a loop with a stop rule
pages.summary: The model may call a tool, read the result, and repeat, until an answer or a cap.

pages.title: Give every tool a name, a schema, and a handler
pages.summary: The model proposes a call. Your code checks the arguments and runs the handler.

pages.title: Allow, deny, and ask a person
pages.summary: Read-only tools can run inside the cap. Anything that leaves the machine waits.

pages.title: Decide what the agent is allowed to remember
pages.summary: The thread, a file, and a store are different lifetimes. Pick one on purpose.

pages.title: Add another agent only when the handoff is a real artifact
pages.summary: Two agents that share a vague chat are one confused loop with extra cost.

pages.title: Read the trace, not the closing summary
pages.summary: Every tool call, argument, result, and approval is a line you can reconstruct.

pages.title: Make tool calls safe to retry, inside a sandbox
pages.summary: A second run of the same call should not double-send, double-charge, or escape the folder.

pages.title: Agents and the Model Context Protocol
pages.summary: An agent, in the sense this lab uses, is a loop: the model may request a tool, your process executes the tool, and the result goes back into the next model call until a stop rule fires. The Model Context Protocol is not that loop. It is a JSON-RPC contract so a host application can talk to many tool servers without inventing a plugin format each time. This room builds both, and it keeps the model from being the thing that runs your code.

pages.title: Multi-agent orchestration
pages.summary: A second model is a second loop, not a second authority. This room says who executes tools, how a budget is split, and why two agents must not both refund.

pages.title: MCP connects a model to tools you did not hard-code
pages.summary: The Model Context Protocol is a standard way for an app to talk to a tool server.

pages.title: Host, client, and server have different jobs
pages.summary: The person uses the host. The client holds the session. The server does the work.

pages.title: Tools act, resources are read, prompts are templates
pages.summary: Use the primitive that matches the risk.

pages.title: Connect a local server over stdio
pages.summary: The host starts a process and speaks MCP on its standard streams. The process is the trust boundary.

pages.title: Consent, authentication, and untrusted servers
pages.summary: A server you did not review can read what the host will hand it, and its tool text can steer the model.

pages.title: How coding tools use MCP
pages.summary: Editors and agents use MCP to reach issue trackers, browsers, docs, and internal APIs. The repo is still reviewed by a person.

pages.title: A coding agent edits a repository under rules
pages.summary: It can read, propose a plan, change files, and run commands. Your rules say which of those happen alone.

pages.title: Give the agent the files and tests that matter
pages.summary: A whole monorepo in the prompt is not context. It is noise.

pages.title: Plan, edit, run, then stop
pages.summary: A plan you can reject is cheaper than a pile of edits you have to unwind.

pages.title: Review the diff and the tests
pages.summary: Read the change as if a new teammate wrote it. Then run the same command they ran.

pages.title: Secrets, destructive git, and the network
pages.summary: The expensive mistakes are not bad indentation.

pages.title: Use a coding agent on a team without shipping junk
pages.summary: Agree the permissions, the review, and what 'the agent did it' does not excuse.

pages.title: An eval is a versioned test, not a feeling
pages.summary: You cannot prefer a new prompt unless the same tasks were scored both times.

pages.title: Start with ten tasks you can explain
pages.summary: A small set you trust beats a large set nobody can audit.

pages.title: Score quality, safety, latency, and cost together
pages.summary: A change that raises quality and doubles the bill needs a decision, not a silent ship.

pages.title: Use a model as a judge only with a rubric and an audit
pages.summary: A judge model is a second system. It has its own failure rate.

pages.title: Gate changes to the prompt, the model, and the index
pages.summary: Each of those is a release. The tasks do not change in the same commit unless the task change is the point.

pages.title: Put red-team cases in the set early
pages.summary: You are checking your own system's boundaries, on inputs you control.

pages.title: Keep the scorecard next to the artifact
pages.summary: A table you can reopen beats a screenshot of one good answer.

pages.title: Evals and observability
pages.summary: A demo is a sample of one. An eval is a decision procedure: named cases, a pass rule written before you look, and a person who may waive a failure in writing. A trace is how you argue about the run afterward. This room builds both, and it refuses to treat a second model as a gold label.

pages.title: Evals and guardrails in production
pages.summary: A golden set runs before you deploy. A sample of live traces runs while the system is in operation. A judge model is a sample, not a gold label. A tool result is text the model will parse, and the host is still the thing that can deny the next call.

pages.title: Fine-tune only after a measured failure of the cheaper fixes
pages.summary: Prompt, schema, retrieval, and tools come first. Training is for a gap those did not close.

pages.title: LoRA trains a small adapter and leaves the base model frozen
pages.summary: QLoRA does the same while the frozen base is stored in a quantized form.

pages.title: Training data has a format, a license, and a leakage problem
pages.summary: Examples teach the behavior. They also teach secrets you forgot were in the log.

pages.title: Compare the adapter to the base model on the same tasks
pages.summary: Keep the adapter only if the scorecard says so, including the tasks that used to pass.

pages.title: Prefer a prompt or a tool when that is the whole gap
pages.summary: Most 'we should fine-tune' reviews end with a schema, a retrieval fix, or a smaller model.

pages.title: Fine-tuning, LoRA, QLoRA, and distillation
pages.summary: A weight update copies the set you trained on. This room says when that copy is the wrong tool, what LoRA and QLoRA actually freeze, how distillation differs from a preference loss, and the eval gate that is allowed to stop the run.

pages.title: Write a one-page safety policy
pages.summary: Name the data, the tools, the actions that need a person, and what you will not build.

pages.title: Decide retention before you log the prompt
pages.summary: Prompts are often personal data. A debug log is a database.

pages.title: A person approves sends, payments, and deletes
pages.summary: Drafting is not the same action as doing.

pages.title: Write an incident note when the model misbehaves
pages.summary: A short note beats a thread of screenshots.

pages.title: What this course will not help you do
pages.summary: The boundary is part of the teaching.

pages.title: AI security and governance
pages.summary: A model will follow the last persuasive string it sees, and a tool will do what the host lets it do. This room names the 2025 OWASP LLM Top 10, assigns NIST’s four functions to a person, and keeps the refund cap in code.

pages.title: Name the job before you name the model
pages.summary: A product sentence has a person, a job, and a constraint. The model is an implementation choice.

pages.title: Write a one-page spec
pages.summary: Problem, user, non-goals, success, risks, and the first milestone.

pages.title: Share four numbers with engineering
pages.summary: Quality, safety fails, latency, and cost per successful task.

pages.title: Design the empty, slow, wrong, and unsafe states
pages.summary: The model will hit all four. The interface should say what happened.

pages.title: Ship a prototype, then an eval, then a limited release
pages.summary: A limited release has a named audience, a kill switch, and a date you will read the scorecard.

pages.title: Add voice only when latency and handoff are designed
pages.summary: Speech recognition and speech synthesis are models with their own failure modes. They do not replace the eval.

pages.title: Choose a capstone you can finish on your own notes
pages.summary: A folder you are allowed to use, questions you wrote, citations, and one read-only tool.

pages.title: Write the acceptance tests before the prompt
pages.summary: If a test is awkward to write, the capstone is still too vague.

pages.title: Keep a build log as you go
pages.summary: Each entry is a run, a trace pointer, a metric, and an artifact.

pages.title: Demo the capstone in ten minutes
pages.summary: Show a pass, a refusal, the trace, and the scorecard. Do not show a tour of the code.

pages.title: Decide the next change from the scorecard
pages.summary: The capstone is finished when you can defend the gate, including a gate that says not yet.

pages.title: Contact center voice AI: the ASR, TTS, and LLM loop
pages.summary: The phone system owns the call. A voice bot is a treatment on that call: something listens, something decides, something speaks, and a human can still be offered the leg. This room draws the loop, a latency budget you can argue about without inventing an industry SLA, and barge-in that stops audio the caller did not hear.

pages.title: AI agents in the contact center
pages.summary: A virtual agent talks to the caller. Agent assist talks to the human who still owns the call. This room names the bridges vendors actually publish — Webex, Amazon Connect, Google CCAI through the Webex connector, and the Microsoft pieces those pages name — and it refuses tenant click-paths, word-error rates, and millisecond budgets this lab did not measure.

pages.title: AI in the contact center ecosystem
pages.summary: A virtual agent talks to the caller. Assist talks to the human. A summary is a draft the human still has to read. Quality management scores the contact later. A forecast predicts volume and handle time. None of those jobs is the phone system, and none of them is allowed to invent a refund. This room names what Webex, Google CCAI, Amazon Connect, and Dynamics 365 actually print about those jobs, retrieved 2026-10-14.

pages.title: Responsible AI and data privacy for voice
pages.summary: A voice bot hears account numbers, records a waveform, and writes a transcript into a log that outlives the call. This room separates redaction, consent, and retention, and it refuses to invent a PCI scope or a retention period the lab did not read.

pages.title: Build a RAG voice agent for a contact center
pages.summary: One design, end to end: a caller asks a question, a retriever packs evidence, a model may request a tool, and a human queue still exists. This room is the architecture, the eval plan, and the rollout. It does not invent a dial plan, a word-error rate, or a millisecond promise.

pages.title: The ecosystem around a system you ship
pages.summary: A shipped assistant borrows a model, an index, a tool loop, a trace, a cloud account, and sometimes a voice stack. None of those own your policy.

pages.title: Architecture from a prompt to a gate
pages.summary: Draw the path before you pick a vendor: input, policy, retrieval, model, tools, trace, and a person at every side effect.

pages.title: Deployment and configuration walkthrough
pages.summary: Configure the run you can roll back: pinned ids, secrets outside the repo, a timeout, a log that omits raw private text, and a kill switch.

pages.title: Migration and cutover from a legacy bot
pages.summary: Move off a rules bot or a pasted FAQ only when the new path wins on a written task set, with a rollback to the old bot.

pages.title: Troubleshooting playbook
pages.summary: Split a bad answer into retrieval, the model, the tool, the policy, and the channel before you change a prompt.

pages.title: Ports, protocols, and a firewall study matrix
pages.summary: Learn the ports this campus actually talks about, then confirm the listener on the host you run. This table is a study matrix, not an ACL to paste into production.

pages.title: Voice bridge: SIP, PSTN, recording, WFM, and emergency calls
pages.summary: The phone system owns the call. A model may transcribe, suggest, or speak only inside the path that system already recorded and routed.

pages.title: CRM, analytics, and API bridges
pages.summary: Integrate by writing a ticket id, a retrieval id, and a tool result into the system of record. Do not paste a customer logo and call it a partnership.

pages.title: AI agents beside a human queue
pages.summary: An agent is a loop with a schema, a step cap, and a trace. In a contact center it sits beside the queue. It does not become the queue.

pages.title: Security, compliance, and the limits of this course
pages.summary: Write the data you will store, the tools you will allow, and the actions that always need a person. This course is not a certification and not legal advice.

pages.title: Roadmap and what was not re-checked
pages.summary: Study the mechanisms. Treat dated product claims as a snapshot unless you open the page.

pages.title: Token
pages.summary: A chunk of text the model reads or writes. Not always a whole word.

pages.title: Context window
pages.summary: The token budget for one request, shared by instructions, sources, conversation, and the answer.

pages.title: Temperature
pages.summary: A sampling control. Lower sticks to likely tokens. Higher lets less likely tokens through.

pages.title: Hallucination
pages.summary: Fluent text that is not grounded in a source, a tool result, or a test you can check.

pages.title: Structured output
pages.summary: A response constrained to a schema, then validated by your code.

pages.title: Embedding
pages.summary: A vector for a piece of text, used for similarity search. Produced by an embedding model, not by the chat model.

pages.title: Chunk
pages.summary: The piece of a document you index, retrieve, and cite.

pages.title: Hybrid search
pages.summary: Keyword search and vector search together, merged into one candidate list.

pages.title: Reranker
pages.summary: A model or rule that reorders a short candidate list for one question.

pages.title: Citation
pages.summary: An id and a span a person can open, attached to a claim.

pages.title: Tool call
pages.summary: A proposed function name and arguments. Your code validates them and runs the handler.

pages.title: Agent
pages.summary: A loop that lets a model call tools, read observations, and stop on a rule you set.

pages.title: MCP
pages.summary: Model Context Protocol. A standard way for a host's client to talk to a server that offers tools, resources, and prompts.

pages.title: MCP host, client, and server
pages.summary: The host is the app a person uses. The client speaks MCP. The server implements the capabilities.

pages.title: Eval
pages.summary: A versioned set of tasks, a scorer, and a record of the model, prompt, and index you ran.

pages.title: Golden set
pages.summary: The small task set you trust enough to gate a change. This course starts at ten tasks you can explain.

pages.title: Judge model
pages.summary: A model that applies a written rubric to an answer. It is a second system, with its own error rate.

pages.title: LoRA
pages.summary: Low-Rank Adaptation. Trains small matrices while the base model stays frozen.

pages.title: Quantization
pages.summary: Storing an existing model's weights in fewer bits so they fit and load faster.

pages.title: Prompt injection
pages.summary: Untrusted text — a page, a ticket, a tool description — that tries to instruct the model.

pages.title: Trace
pages.summary: The ordered record of tool calls, arguments, results, approvals, and stops.

pages.title: Human approval
pages.summary: A person confirms the exact arguments of a side effect before the handler runs.

pages.title: Coding agent
pages.summary: An agent whose tools read and edit a repository and may run commands you allowed.

pages.title: Allowlist
pages.summary: The tools or commands that may run. Everything else is denied.

pages.title: Logit
pages.summary: A score over the vocabulary before softmax. Temperature divides logits in the sampler, not inside attention.

pages.title: Softmax
pages.summary: Turns scores into a distribution that sums to one. The scale in attention is there so softmax does not saturate.

pages.title: Nucleus sampling
pages.summary: Holtzman: keep the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds p.

pages.title: Top-p
pages.summary: The nucleus threshold. Alter top-p or temperature, not both, on OpenAI chat completions.

pages.title: Logprobs
pages.summary: Log probability of chosen tokens. On chat completions, top_logprobs requires logprobs true.

pages.title: Seed
pages.summary: Chat Completions beta: best-effort determinism when other parameters match. Not a guarantee. Watch system_fingerprint.

pages.title: Max_completion_tokens
pages.summary: Chat Completions cap on generated tokens, including reasoning tokens. max_tokens is documented as deprecated.

pages.title: Max_output_tokens
pages.summary: Responses API cap named in the token-counting guide. It counts generated tokens, including ones you do not see.

pages.title: Attention
pages.summary: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V in Vaswani et al. Historical architecture, not a 2026 score.

pages.title: Causal mask
pages.summary: Stops a position from attending to future tokens. The paper masks illegal connections before softmax.

pages.title: KV cache
pages.summary: Reuse of past keys and values across decoding steps. Check the serving stack you run. Cache bytes vary with length, layers, precision, and batch.

pages.title: Tokenizer
pages.summary: Maps text to integer ids. The lab visualizer is a teaching merge table, not a provider tokenizer.

pages.title: Greedy decoding
pages.summary: Take the highest logit each step. Temperature 0 is not documented on the fetched pages as a proof of greedy argmax.

pages.title: Top-k
pages.summary: Keep the k highest tokens before sampling. Distinct from nucleus (top-p), which keeps a probability mass.

pages.title: Detokenize
pages.summary: Map chosen ids back to text. The last stage of the inference picture in T1.

pages.title: BPE
pages.summary: Byte-pair encoding: merge frequent pairs. The lab’s merge table is a toy, not a provider tokenizer.

pages.title: Residual
pages.summary: A skip connection around a sublayer. Vaswani et al. use it so the stack can add to the previous representation.

pages.title: Feed-forward
pages.summary: The position-wise network after attention in the 2017 block. Not the retrieval index.

pages.title: Decoder-only
pages.summary: A stack that predicts the next token with a causal mask. The usual shape of a chat model.

pages.title: System_fingerprint
pages.summary: The field you watch when you use Chat Completions seed. Seed is best-effort, not a guarantee.

pages.title: Knowledge cutoff
pages.summary: The date a model card claims its training knowledge ends. Astra and Sol were 30 April 2026 on the platform page.

pages.title: Short context
pages.summary: On the OpenAI pricing page fetched 2026-10-14, standard short context means at most 272k input tokens.

pages.title: Batch API
pages.summary: A cheaper asynchronous tier. gpt-6-astra short-context batch was $5 / $25 per million tokens that day.

pages.title: Regional processing
pages.summary: The pricing page says eligible models released on or after 5 March 2026 take a 10% uplift. Dated 2026-10-14.

pages.title: Haiku
pages.summary: claude-haiku-5-5, from $0.10 / $0.50 per million tokens on Anthropic’s models page, 1M context.

pages.title: Opus
pages.summary: claude-opus-5-5 at $4 / $20 per million tokens, 1M context, 128k max output, on that same page.

pages.title: Argon
pages.summary: gemini-4-argon, Google’s flagship on the models page updated 2026-10-13. Unified 1M context.

pages.title: Instruction hierarchy
pages.summary: OpenAI’s text guide: instructions take priority over input. That sentence is not a proof against prompt injection.

pages.title: Few-shot
pages.summary: Brown et al.: demonstrations in the text, no gradient update. GPT-3’s 175B and its scores are historical.

pages.title: Chain-of-thought
pages.summary: Wei et al.: exemplars that include intermediate reasoning steps. The PaLM 540B GSM8K figure is historical.

pages.title: Indirect injection
pages.summary: Untrusted text that arrives inside a retrieved page, an email, or a tool result, not only in the user box.

pages.title: Instruction
pages.summary: The channel OpenAI’s text guide says takes priority over input. Priority is not an injection proof.

pages.title: Zero-shot
pages.summary: The task is stated with no demonstrations. It is not an empty prompt.

pages.title: Prompt version
pages.summary: The instruction text, the model id, and the eval set that must pass before that version ships.

pages.title: JSON schema
pages.summary: A shape constraint. A valid object can still be the wrong decision.

pages.title: Strict mode
pages.summary: On the structured-outputs guide, strict true asks the API to follow the schema. It does not authorize a refund.

pages.title: Untrusted text
pages.summary: Retrieved pages, mail, and tool results. Label them as data.

pages.title: Few-shot exemplar
pages.summary: A demonstration in the text. Brown et al. used them with no gradient. Historical scores stay historical.

pages.title: Refusal
pages.summary: A deliberate non-answer. Distinct from a crash and from a hallucinated policy.

pages.title: RAG
pages.summary: Lewis et al. 2020 named retrieval-augmented generation. Production retrieve-then-read is not their training recipe.

pages.title: Parametric memory
pages.summary: Knowledge in the weights. In the 2020 paper, that was BART-large, about 400M parameters. Historical.

pages.title: Cosine distance
pages.summary: pgvector <=> is cosine distance. Similarity is 1 minus that distance. HNSW cosine uses vector_cosine_ops.

pages.title: Vector(n)
pages.summary: pgvector README examples use embedding vector(3). You may also store an unfixed vector and cast.

pages.title: Chunking
pages.summary: Split documents so a retriever can return the passage that answers. No universal size is cited.

pages.title: Recall
pages.summary: Did the gold chunk appear in the top k? A fluency score does not answer that.

pages.title: Abstention
pages.summary: OpenAI’s embeddings QA sketch: if the article lacks the answer, say you do not know.

pages.title: HNSW
pages.summary: A graph index. pgvector’s cosine HNSW uses vector_cosine_ops. The index does not check which model wrote the vector.

pages.title: Inner product
pages.summary: pgvector <#> is the negative inner product. ASC then ranks the largest inner product first.

pages.title: L2 distance
pages.summary: pgvector <-> with vector_l2_ops. Switching to it does not repair a mixed embedding model.

pages.title: Metadata filter
pages.summary: A predicate beside the vector search, such as language or product. It is not a substitute for the right model id.

pages.title: Chunk overlap
pages.summary: Characters or tokens repeated between neighboring chunks. No universal size is cited.

pages.title: Embedding model id
pages.summary: The string recorded on every row. Query vectors must come from the same id.

pages.title: Freshness
pages.summary: Whether the index matches the source that changed on Tuesday. A fine-tune will not track that PDF.

pages.title: Cosine similarity
pages.summary: 1 minus pgvector cosine distance, for vectors from the same model. The embedding lab computes it on numbers you type.

pages.title: Dot product
pages.summary: The sum of pairwise products. It grows with vector length, unlike cosine.

pages.title: Pgvector
pages.summary: A Postgres extension. <=> cosine, <-> L2, <#> negative inner product, <+> L1.

pages.title: LlamaIndex
pages.summary: A framework whose overview, fetched 2026-10-14, says MIT and defaults document indexing to OpenAI embeddings.

pages.title: Vector store ingest
pages.summary: OpenAI’s rate-limits guide, fetched 2026-10-14, lists 300 RPM per vector store id for file ingest.

pages.title: LlamaParse
pages.summary: The hosted parser the LlamaIndex overview says was formerly LlamaCloud.

pages.title: Tools/call
pages.summary: MCP request that runs a tool. Consent for side effects comes before this call.

pages.title: ReAct
pages.summary: Yao et al.: interleave reasoning and actions. ALFWorld and WebShop gains are historical, not an SLA.

pages.title: Idempotency
pages.summary: A key your server understands so a retry does not refund twice. The MCP spec’s call shape does not invent that key for you.

pages.title: Host
pages.summary: The application that executes tools. MCP revision 2025-11-25 keeps execution here.

pages.title: MCP client
pages.summary: The protocol peer inside the host that talks to a server. Not the language model.

pages.title: MCP server
pages.summary: The peer that declares tools. Its descriptions are untrusted.

pages.title: JSON-RPC
pages.summary: The message shape MCP uses. A tool call is a request, not a side effect by itself.

pages.title: Consent
pages.summary: A human or a rule before a side effect. Another agent agreeing is not consent.

pages.title: Allow-list
pages.summary: The tools a given bot may receive. Inheritance from a copied bot is excessive agency.

pages.title: LangGraph
pages.summary: LangChain’s overview calls it the low-level orchestration framework for deterministic and agentic workflows.

pages.title: AutoGen
pages.summary: Wu et al.: conversable agents, tools, and humans, patterns in language or code. Historical. Not an SLA.

pages.title: Create_agent
pages.summary: LangChain constructor: model, tools, system_prompt. A framework call is not a security boundary.

pages.title: Multi-agent
pages.summary: Several model loops and one host. A second speaker is not a second authority.

pages.title: Router
pages.summary: A model or a rule that picks an intent. In this lab its tool list is empty.

pages.title: Specialist
pages.summary: The one loop allowed to request a side-effect tool for that intent.

pages.title: Step budget
pages.summary: Max model calls per agent and per user turn. Chatter is tokens.

pages.title: Reviewer agent
pages.summary: A commenter. If it holds post_refund, it is not a reviewer.

pages.title: Idempotency key
pages.summary: Your server’s name for one side effect. A retry with the same key must not post twice.

pages.title: Workflow
pages.summary: LlamaIndex describes workflows as event-driven. An event is not an approval.

pages.title: Gen_ai.operation.name
pages.summary: OpenTelemetry registry key. Example values include chat, embeddings, execute_tool, retrieval. The page says the attributes moved.

pages.title: Faithfulness
pages.summary: Whether the answer stayed inside the passages you packed. Distinct from whether the retriever found them.

pages.title: Trajectory eval
pages.summary: Grade the tool path, not only the last sentence. A correct refund sentence after two charges still fails.

pages.title: AI RMF
pages.summary: NIST AI 100-1, voluntary, published 26 January 2023. Core functions: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage.

pages.title: LLM-as-judge
pages.summary: A second model can grade and can share the first model’s blind spots. It is not a gold label.

pages.title: Span
pages.summary: One named operation in a trace. execute_tool should appear once per refund.

pages.title: Waiver
pages.summary: A named owner and an expiry. Silent “known flake” comments are not waivers.

pages.title: Grader
pages.summary: A rule or a model that scores a case. Money cases prefer a rule.

pages.title: Context recall
pages.summary: Whether the gold passage was in the pack. Distinct from faithfulness of the wording.

pages.title: Online eval
pages.summary: A check while the system is in operation. NIST says test regularly then. Unlabeled traffic is not a pass rate.

pages.title: CI gate
pages.summary: The build fails when a pinned prompt or a trajectory regresses.

pages.title: LangSmith
pages.summary: The product LangChain’s overview names for traces, debugging, and evaluation. No numeric quota was on that page.

pages.title: Rubric
pages.summary: The pass rule a human can audit. The rubric lab scores cases locally. A model is not the judge there.

pages.title: OpenTelemetry
pages.summary: The trace standard. GenAI attribute names in this lab are pinned to commit 4e8a281.

pages.title: Trajectory
pages.summary: The ordered tool path. Two commits and a polite sentence still fail.

pages.title: Prompt hash
pages.summary: The identity of the instruction text on the run record. Rollback returns to a previous hash.

pages.title: QLoRA
pages.summary: LoRA on a 4-bit frozen base. NF4, double quantization, paged optimizers. Dettmers et al.

pages.title: NF4
pages.summary: 4-bit NormalFloat, QLoRA’s type for the frozen base. Not a rank.

pages.title: Distillation
pages.summary: A student learns a teacher’s mapping. Hinton, Vinyals, and Dean. The teacher must already pass.

pages.title: DPO
pages.summary: A classification loss on preference pairs. Rafailov et al. say it removes a separate RL loop. Historical.

pages.title: RLHF
pages.summary: The pipeline DPO rewrites: a reward model, then a reinforcement-learning fine-tune. Not the same file as supervised pairs.

pages.title: Rank
pages.summary: The inner dimension of a LoRA update. The paper’s r of 1 or 2 is their example, not your default.

pages.title: Adapter
pages.summary: The small file you can unload. Merging makes rollback a full checkpoint restore.

pages.title: Frozen weights
pages.summary: The base you do not train. QLoRA quantizes them. The license file is still theirs.

pages.title: Train leakage
pages.summary: Golden rows inside the train file. The perfect score is memory.

pages.title: Eval gate
pages.summary: Prompt baseline versus adapter on the same cases. A tie means you do not ship the weights.

pages.title: Preference pair
pages.summary: Prompt, chosen, rejected. If both are wrong, the loss still prefers the chosen one.

pages.title: Double quantization
pages.summary: QLoRA’s second memory idea: quantize the quantization constants. Dettmers et al.

pages.title: Paged optimizer
pages.summary: QLoRA’s third memory idea, meant to absorb activation spikes. Not a serving format.

pages.title: Merge
pages.summary: Fold a LoRA into the base so the forward pass has no extra latency. Do it after rollback is rehearsed.

pages.title: Soft label
pages.summary: The teacher’s distribution over wrong answers, which Hinton et al. say the student should learn.

pages.title: Hard label
pages.summary: A single target token. Distilling only hard labels can drop abstention.

pages.title: ASR
pages.summary: Automatic speech recognition. In a cascaded bot it writes the text the language model sees.

pages.title: TTS
pages.summary: Text-to-speech. It speaks the reply. Barge-in must stop playback and tell the session what was actually heard.

pages.title: Barge-in
pages.summary: The caller talks over the bot. OpenAI Realtime: cancel the response and truncate unplayed audio.

pages.title: Server VAD
pages.summary: OpenAI Realtime turn detection. The VAD guide’s example sets interrupt_response and a silence duration. Those numbers are an example, not your SLA.

pages.title: Latency budget
pages.summary: A worksheet that names the hops. Check your own traces. The time varies with region, model, and tool hops.

pages.title: Containment
pages.summary: The bot finished the call without a human. That is not the same as a resolved customer problem.

pages.title: Handoff packet
pages.summary: What the human agent must see in the first seconds: intent, identity already checked, and what was promised.

pages.title: VAD
pages.summary: Voice activity detection. The server-VAD guide’s silence figure is an example, not your SLA.

pages.title: Endpointing
pages.summary: Deciding the caller has finished a turn. If this time is flat, a latency spike is elsewhere.

pages.title: ACD
pages.summary: The phone system that queues and routes. The model is a treatment, not the ACD.

pages.title: Transfer
pages.summary: Hand the caller to a human. The handoff packet says what was already promised.

pages.title: Agent assist
pages.summary: Suggestions on a human’s desktop. The human still owns the call.

pages.title: Truncate
pages.summary: Drop unplayed audio from the model’s context when the caller barges in.

pages.title: WER
pages.summary: Word error rate of a recognizer. Not cited as a universal number in this lab.

pages.title: LLM01
pages.summary: Prompt injection, OWASP 2025. RAG and fine-tuning do not fully mitigate it.

pages.title: LLM02
pages.summary: Sensitive information disclosure.

pages.title: LLM03
pages.summary: Supply chain: model, data, package, plugin.

pages.title: LLM04
pages.summary: Data and model poisoning, including fine-tuning and embedding data.

pages.title: LLM05
pages.summary: Improper output handling. Do not pass model text into SQL, a shell, or a dial string.

pages.title: LLM06
pages.summary: Excessive agency. Too many tools, or two agents that can both refund.

pages.title: LLM07
pages.summary: System prompt leakage. Do not store a key in the prompt.

pages.title: LLM08
pages.summary: Vector and embedding weaknesses.

pages.title: LLM09
pages.summary: Misinformation, with or without an attacker.

pages.title: LLM10
pages.summary: Unbounded consumption: tokens, loops, and retries.

pages.title: Govern
pages.summary: The NIST function that names who may change a tool or waive a case.

pages.title: Map
pages.summary: The NIST function for context: who is affected and what can go wrong.

pages.title: Measure
pages.summary: Test before deployment and regularly in operation.

pages.title: Manage
pages.summary: Respond, recover, communicate. The kill switch lives here.

pages.title: Kill switch
pages.summary: Disable the tool and restore the previous prompt hash.

pages.title: Redaction
pages.summary: Keep the raw system prompt and payment data out of the trace. Store hashes.

pages.title: Supply chain
pages.summary: Every artifact you did not author. Pin ids. A framework’s MIT line is not a weight license.

pages.title: Poisoning
pages.summary: A manipulated article, embed, or train row. LLM04.

pages.title: NIST AI 100-1
pages.summary: AI RMF 1.0, 26 January 2023, voluntary, being revised.

pages.title: NIST AI 600-1
pages.summary: Generative AI Profile, 26 July 2024, as the AI RMF overview states. Subcategory codes stay unread here.

pages.title: Article hash
pages.summary: The identity of a help-center page. A changed hash is how you notice an injected paragraph.

pages.title: Query matrix
pages.summary: Q in Attention(Q, K, V). It is the attention query, not the retrieval query.

pages.title: Key matrix
pages.summary: K in the 2017 attention formula. The scale is the square root of the key dimension.

pages.title: Value matrix
pages.summary: V in scaled dot-product attention. Softmax weights mix these rows.

pages.title: Multi-head attention
pages.summary: Several attention maps in parallel, then concatenated. One head is not the reason for a sentence.

pages.title: Scaled dot-product
pages.summary: QK transpose divided by the square root of the key dimension, before softmax, so the scores do not saturate.

pages.title: Positional encoding
pages.summary: How the 2017 paper told the model where a token sits. A match with sinusoids was not a measured promise of longer windows.

pages.title: Next-token prediction
pages.summary: The training task of a decoder-only model: predict the next id given the past.

pages.title: Responses API
pages.summary: OpenAI’s text guide, fetched 2026-10-14, says to use Responses for text generation and prefers it to Chat Completions.

pages.title: Chat Completions
pages.summary: The older text API. The same guide says new text work should use Responses.

pages.title: Output_text
pages.summary: An SDK helper that joins text items. The guide says not to assume the text sits at the first output item.

pages.title: Model snapshot
pages.summary: The text guide retrieved 2026-10-14 prints: pin production to specific model snapshots (like gpt-5.5-2026-04-23 for example). The habit is the pin. The id in parentheses is their example.

pages.title: Reasoning effort
pages.summary: A Responses field on the fetched text guide, shown as low beside gpt-6-astra. It is not a latency target.

pages.title: Developer role
pages.summary: On the fetched Responses guide, a developer message is the application’s instruction and ranks ahead of the user message.

pages.title: Previous_response_id
pages.summary: Conversation state on Responses. The text guide says instructions from earlier turns are not carried by this id.

pages.title: Vocabulary
pages.summary: The set of ids the sampler chooses from. Softmax is over this set, not over words.

pages.title: Argmax
pages.summary: Pick the largest score. The fetched chat-completions page does not say temperature 0 is argmax.

pages.title: Hidden state
pages.summary: The vector inside the stack. Check the endpoint reference you call. Whether internals are returned varies by product.

pages.title: BLEU
pages.summary: The 2014 translation scores in the sequence-to-sequence paper. Historical test numbers, not a current model claim.

pages.title: IRoPE
pages.summary: Named on the Llama 4 materials fetched 2026-10-14. The room does not treat the blog as a serving target.

pages.title: Special token
pages.summary: An id the chat template adds, such as a role marker. It still counts against the window.

pages.title: Prompt cache
pages.summary: OpenAI’s data-controls page says encrypted key and value tensors can sit in GPU-local storage and then expire. That is not a correctness guarantee.

pages.title: Safety identifier
pages.summary: A hashed user or session string on the safety guide fetched 2026-10-14. It is not the user’s email.

pages.title: Gpt-6-astra
pages.summary: Printed as model gpt-6-astra in the text-guide code samples retrieved 2026-10-14. Copy the id from the page you open, then pin a snapshot. Do not memorize this string.

pages.title: Input parameter
pages.summary: The Responses field the text guide ranks below instructions. User text belongs here.

pages.title: Delimiter
pages.summary: A fence around untrusted text. It is a label, not a proof the model will obey it.

pages.title: Example hash
pages.summary: The identity of the few-shot block. Changing examples is a release even when the instruction sentence is identical.

pages.title: Schema version
pages.summary: The identity of the JSON shape you asked for. A valid object can still be the wrong decision.

pages.title: Parallel tool calls
pages.summary: A product switch on tool calling. This lab does not state the default of a snapshot it has not re-read.

pages.title: AdditionalProperties
pages.summary: A JSON Schema keyword. This lab does not copy a blog’s rule for it. Re-read the guide on the day you code.

pages.title: Tool name regex
pages.summary: Anthropic’s fetched page constrains tool names to one to sixty-four characters from a limited set.

pages.title: Saved prompt object
pages.summary: The text guide retrieved 2026-10-14 prints: Prompt creation will be de-emphasized beginning June 3, 2026, and v1/prompts is scheduled to shut down on November 30, 2026. Keep prompts in code.

pages.title: Shot count
pages.summary: How many demonstrations you include. Brown et al. do not name an optimal count for a contact center.

pages.title: Data channel
pages.summary: Retrieved text, mail, and tool results. Label them as data so they are not read as instructions.

pages.title: Assistant role
pages.summary: On the fetched Responses guide, messages the model generated have the assistant role.

pages.title: User role
pages.summary: End-user text on the Responses guide. It ranks behind developer messages.

pages.title: BM25
pages.summary: A lexical score. Hybrid search puts it beside a vector index, then fuses the lists.

pages.title: RRF
pages.summary: Reciprocal rank fusion. It merges ranked lists. It does not recover a gold chunk the first stage dropped.

pages.title: IVFFlat
pages.summary: A list index named beside HNSW in the hybrid-search room. The index does not check the embedding model id.

pages.title: Dense retrieval
pages.summary: Search by a query vector. The query and the rows must share an embedding model id.

pages.title: Sparse retrieval
pages.summary: Search by lexical overlap, such as BM25 or tsvector. Proper nouns often live here.

pages.title: Document hash
pages.summary: The identity of a source version. Without it you cannot delete a stale article.

pages.title: Chunk id
pages.summary: The pointer the answer must cite. Fluency without ids cannot be graded.

pages.title: Pack
pages.summary: The passages you actually put in the prompt. Faithfulness is judged against the pack, not the whole corpus.

pages.title: Neighbor count
pages.summary: How many rows the vector search returns. This lab does not publish a magic k.

pages.title: Audience filter
pages.summary: A metadata predicate that keeps another customer’s notes out of the pack.

pages.title: Tsvector
pages.summary: Postgres full text. The hybrid-search room names it as the lexical side of an index.

pages.title: Grounding
pages.summary: The answer stays inside the packed passages. A fluent sentence with no chunk id is not grounded.

pages.title: Re-embed
pages.summary: Write new vectors after a model change. A region move that changes the embedding model is an outage you caused.

pages.title: Delete by document id
pages.summary: The operation that removes every chunk of one source. Deleting one vector row is not enough.

pages.title: Resources
pages.summary: An MCP server feature in revision 2025-11-25: context and data for the user or the model.

pages.title: MCP prompts
pages.summary: Templated messages a server offers in revision 2025-11-25. They are not a substitute for the host’s consent check.

pages.title: Sampling
pages.summary: A client feature in the 2025-11-25 spec: the server asks the client to run a model. The user must approve.

pages.title: Roots
pages.summary: A client feature: the server asks which URI or filesystem boundary it may use.

pages.title: Elicitation
pages.summary: A client feature in revision 2025-11-25: the server asks the user for more information.

pages.title: Tools/list
pages.summary: The MCP request that returns tool declarations. A huge list is a token problem, not a reason to skip consent.

pages.title: Tool description
pages.summary: Revision 2025-11-25 says descriptions are untrusted unless the server is trusted.

pages.title: Stdio
pages.summary: A local MCP connection. It has no public route. An HTTP server needs a network policy.

pages.title: Streamable HTTP
pages.summary: An MCP transport. A public listener without authentication is an incident.

pages.title: Tool_choice
pages.summary: The provider field that steers whether a tool is offered or required. The host still executes.

pages.title: Side effect
pages.summary: A tool that changes the world: a refund, a transfer, a write. Consent comes before it runs.

pages.title: Argument validation
pages.summary: The host checks the JSON before the tool runs. A schema match is not an authorization.

pages.title: Baseline
pages.summary: The previous prompt hash on the same cases. A new prompt ships only if it does not lose to this.

pages.title: Regression
pages.summary: A case that used to pass and now fails. The CI gate exists for this.

pages.title: Pass rule
pages.summary: The sentence a human can audit. Money cases prefer a rule over a second model.

pages.title: Flake
pages.summary: An unstable case. A comment that says known flake is not a waiver with an owner and an expiry.

pages.title: Pinned revision
pages.summary: The GenAI conventions commit this lab names: 4e8a281 on 2026-10-13. Copying a name without the pin breaks quietly.

pages.title: Execute_tool
pages.summary: A gen_ai.operation.name value on the pinned tree. One refund should produce one such span.

pages.title: Retrieval span
pages.summary: The trace row for the pack. If it is missing, you cannot tell a retrieval miss from a wording miss.

pages.title: Production sample
pages.summary: A slice of live traffic you chose a rate for. Customers are not an unlabeled test set.

pages.title: Judge agreement
pages.summary: How often a model judge matches a human. This lab does not publish a target percentage.

pages.title: Harm list
pages.summary: The Map step before you pick cases: money, identity, transfer, and injection.

pages.title: Checkpoint
pages.summary: A saved copy of weights. Merging an adapter means rollback is restoring this, not unloading a file.

pages.title: Rollback
pages.summary: Return to the previous prompt hash or the previous checkpoint. Rehearse it before you merge.

pages.title: Held-out set
pages.summary: Rows the train file must not contain. A perfect score on leaked rows is memory.

pages.title: Supervised pair
pages.summary: A prompt and a target completion. It is not a preference pair and it is not a reward model.

pages.title: Reward model
pages.summary: The model RLHF trains to score outputs. The DPO paper says it removes a separate reinforcement-learning loop.

pages.title: Cascade
pages.summary: Speech recognition, then the language model, then speech synthesis. Each hop is a failure domain you can time.

pages.title: Speech-to-speech
pages.summary: The Realtime guide’s session: the model takes audio, keeps state, and can call tools.

pages.title: Jitter buffer
pages.summary: The telephony edge hides packet loss. A laptop demo does not measure it.

pages.title: Conversation.item.truncate
pages.summary: The Realtime event that drops audio the caller did not hear.

pages.title: Resolution
pages.summary: The problem stayed fixed. Containment only says a human did not take the call.

pages.title: Pack miss
pages.summary: A transfer reason this lab logs when it does not have the tenant’s reason-code catalog.

pages.title: Media edge
pages.summary: Where the caller’s audio actually terminates. Measure latency there, not only in the browser.

pages.title: Playback buffer
pages.summary: Audio already generated and not yet played. Truncate it when the caller barges in.

pages.title: Storage limitation
pages.summary: GDPR Article 5(1)(e): identifiable data kept no longer than necessary. Not a universal day count.

pages.title: Purpose limitation
pages.summary: GDPR Article 5(1)(b): a recording notice is not a training purpose.

pages.title: Data minimisation
pages.summary: GDPR Article 5(1)(c): adequate, relevant, and limited to the purpose.

pages.title: PCI DSS
pages.summary: PCI SSC’s page: a baseline for entities that store, process, or transmit cardholder or sensitive authentication data.

pages.title: QSA
pages.summary: A Qualified Security Assessor. This lab does not assign PCI scope.

pages.title: Cardholder data
pages.summary: What PCI DSS is written to protect. A full card number stays out of the model, the log, and the pane.

pages.title: Zero Data Retention
pages.summary: An OpenAI approval, not the default. The fetched default abuse-monitoring window is up to 30 days.

pages.title: Abuse monitoring
pages.summary: OpenAI logs that can contain API prompts and responses, retained up to 30 days by default on the page fetched 2026-10-14.

pages.title: CCPA deletion
pages.summary: The California Attorney General’s page: respond in 45 calendar days, extendable by another 45. A response window, not a retention period.

pages.title: Consent event
pages.summary: A record that the stated purpose was played. If barge-in cut it off, the event is interrupted, not granted.

pages.title: PAN
pages.summary: A primary account number. It does not belong in a prompt, a trace, or a fixture.

pages.title: Sink
pages.summary: One place a fact is stored: recording, transcript, case, trace, provider log, or eval copy.

pages.title: Non-parametric memory
pages.summary: The 2020 RAG paper’s name for an index you can replace when facts change, beside the parametric generator.

pages.title: RAG-Sequence
pages.summary: Lewis et al. marginalize retrieved documents once per output sequence. A historical training recipe, not a 2026 API flag.

pages.title: RAG-Token
pages.summary: The same paper’s per-token marginalization over retrieved documents. Do not cite it as a contact-center latency number.

pages.title: Bi-encoder
pages.summary: The RAG paper initializes its retriever from Dense Passage Retrieval, a bi-encoder. Query and document are embedded separately.

pages.title: Retrieve-then-read
pages.summary: What teams usually mean by RAG now: a frozen chat model, an embeddings API, a vector index, and an abstain instruction.

pages.title: Vector_cosine_ops
pages.summary: The pgvector operator class for an HNSW index on cosine distance. Cosine similarity is one minus the <=> distance.

pages.title: Dimensions
pages.summary: An embeddings API parameter, on text-embedding-3 and later, that shortens a vector. Query and document widths still have to match.

pages.title: Ef_search
pages.summary: The HNSW query-time candidate list. The pgvector README’s filtering section mentions a default of 40 and an example of 100.

pages.title: Ef_construction
pages.summary: The HNSW build-time candidate list. The README example this room cites is 64, beside m = 16. It is an example, not a tuned index.

pages.title: Probes
pages.summary: How many IVFFlat lists a query searches. The README says to start near sqrt(lists). probes equal to lists is exact and may skip the index.

pages.title: Iterative scan

pages.title: Rank_constant

pages.title: Rank_window_size

pages.title: Cross-encoder

pages.title: K1

pages.title: Discount_overlaps
pages.summary: An Elasticsearch BM25 switch, default true on the 8.19 page. It is not a pgvector setting.

pages.title: Partial index

pages.title: Text-embedding-3-small

pages.title: Text-embedding-3-large

pages.title: Strict_order

pages.title: Lost in the middle

pages.title: Tool_use

pages.title: Stop_reason

pages.summary: A tool you execute after the model requests it. Anthropic’s docs split these from server tools the vendor executes.

pages.title: Server tool
