pages.title: How do you decide to fine-tune?
pages.summary: Exclude the cheaper fixes with an eval, then train only for the gap that remains.

pages.title: How do you evaluate a prompt or model change?
pages.summary: Same tasks, four numbers, a gate you wrote beforehand.

pages.title: How do you stop an agent from doing damage?
pages.summary: An allowlist, a step cap, validated arguments, and a person on side effects.

pages.title: What is MCP, and when would you use it?
pages.summary: A protocol for connecting a host to a tool server, when more than one app should share that server.

pages.title: How do you review a coding agent's change?
pages.summary: Read the diff, rerun the tests, and reject hunks that do not serve the goal.

pages.title: How do you control cost and latency?
pages.summary: Smaller context, a cheaper model where the eval allows it, caps, and cost per successful task.

pages.title: How do you know a grounded answer is not invented?
pages.summary: The citation has to be an id you retrieved, and some tasks must refuse.

pages.title: What goes in an AI product spec?
pages.summary: The job, the non-goals, the four numbers, the failure states, and the kill switch.

pages.title: 1. What is a language model?
pages.summary: A language model scores the next token given the tokens so far. A sampler picks one, you append it, and you repeat. The product wrapped around that loop is a message API. The model is not a database and not a search engine.

pages.title: 2. Explain attention without a whiteboard full of letters.
pages.summary: Each position builds a query, keys, and values. The query’s match to each key becomes a weight after scaling and softmax. The output is the weighted sum of the values. A causal mask zeroes out the future.

pages.title: 3. What do temperature and top-p actually change?
pages.summary: Both reshape the distribution the network already produced. Temperature divides logits before softmax. Top-p keeps the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities sum past a threshold, then renormalizes. I change one, not both.

pages.title: 4. The model already “knows” a lot. Why retrieve anything?
pages.summary: Weights are a lossy memory with no update button and no citation. Retrieval puts a source in the window and lets you swap the source when the fact changes. That is the split the RAG paper named: parametric versus non-parametric memory.

pages.title: 5. Where does this sit on a contact-center call?
pages.summary: The ACD owns the call. Speech-to-text writes the user message. The model samples the reply or a tool request. Text-to-speech speaks it. Transfer is a route, not a token. I do not let the model become a second phone system.

pages.title: Write attention in one line.
pages.summary: Weighted sum of values. Weights from scaled query–key dots, then softmax.

pages.title: Why the square root?
pages.summary: The paper’s gradient motive as dimension grows. You can also show the toy.

pages.title: Decoder versus encoder.
pages.summary: Decoder self-attention is causal. Encoder self-attention in the paper is not. Chat is often decoder-only.

pages.title: How many heads does Scout have?
pages.summary: The card does not say. It says 16 experts and 17B active parameters.

pages.title: What is iRoPE?
pages.summary: The blog’s positional story for Llama 4, including RoPE and layers without positions.

pages.title: Is Scout’s context 256K or 10M?
pages.summary: Both sentences. The card’s context field is 10M. The blog says Scout was pre-trained and post-trained at 256K, which empowers length generalization, and it also names a 10M supported context.

pages.title: Is temperature 0 greedy argmax?
pages.summary: The chat-completions page does not say that. It documents a temperature between 0 and 2 and recommends altering temperature or top_p, but not both. It does not forbid sending both.

pages.title: What is Lost in the Middle?
pages.summary: A U-shaped result: relevant information at the beginning or the end is used more than the same information in the middle. arXiv:2307.03172. Not a Scout measurement.

pages.title: 1. What is the difference between an instruction and a guarantee?
pages.summary: An instruction is text in a channel the provider may rank above the user. A guarantee is a check that still holds when the model ignores the text. I cite the instructions-over-input sentence, and I put caps in tools.

pages.title: 2. When do you add examples, and when do you add chain-of-thought?
pages.summary: Examples when the shape is wrong. Chain-of-thought when a human must see steps and I still grade the decision separately. Neither one inserts a missing document.

pages.title: 3. A retrieved article tells the bot to ignore a cap. Walk the incident.
pages.summary: Indirect injection. The article is parsed text. I label it untrusted, I keep the cap in the tool, and I add the article to the golden set. I do not only lengthen the system prompt.

pages.title: 4. How do you version a prompt?
pages.summary: Separate files for instruction, examples, and schema. Hash them. Pin the model id. Gate the bundle with an eval. Roll back by hash, not by memory.

pages.title: 5. Where does prompting sit on a phone call?
pages.summary: ASR writes the user channel. The instruction file is still just text. The ACD owns transfer. I do not let a prompt become a second dial plan.

pages.title: 1. Is JSON schema an authorization system?
pages.summary: No. It constrains shape on the models the guide names. The tool and the policy check authorize the side effect. A valid refund object can still be over the cap.

pages.title: 2. Walk a tool call without waving at “the agent.”
pages.summary: Send tools. Receive a call. Execute in the application. Return the output with the call id. Stop, or handle another call. The model does not run the function.

pages.title: 3. The hours bot refunded someone. Where do you look first?
pages.summary: The tool list on that bot. Then the host check. Then the prompt. A sentence that says “do not refund” loses to a registered function.

pages.title: 4. How do you keep a second vendor from inheriting the first vendor’s JSON?
pages.summary: Separate adapters. OpenAI’s text.format is not an Anthropic field. A shared create_agent call is not a shared schema.

pages.title: 1. How do you stop prompt injection?
pages.summary: I don’t, not fully. LLM01 says RAG and fine-tuning don’t either. I keep untrusted text labeled, I strip tools the bot should not have, and I enforce the cap in the host.

pages.title: 2. The hours bot refunded someone. Where do you look first?
pages.summary: The tool list. Then the host check. Then the packed article. A sentence that says “do not refund” loses to a registered function.

pages.title: 3. What does SEP-1577 change about who runs the tool?
pages.summary: It doesn’t. The line adds tools and toolChoice parameters on sampling. The host still mediates. The model still does not execute.

pages.title: 4. A schema-valid refund comes back. What do you do with it?
pages.summary: I parse it, then I run the cap. Strict mode made the shape more reliable. It did not authorize the money.

pages.title: 1. Design a grounded assistant. Start wherever you want.
pages.summary: I separate ingest from query. Ingest chunks documents, embeds them with a pinned model, and stores vectors with ids and filters. Query embeds the question with that same model, filters, packs a few chunks with ids, and accepts an answer only when every cited id was packed. Otherw

pages.title: 2. What did the RAG paper contribute that a tutorial often skips?
pages.summary: A probabilistic model. Retrieved documents are latent. RAG-Sequence shares one document across the output. RAG-Token can switch per token. They fine-tuned the query encoder and BART and froze the document index.

pages.title: 3. A retrieval demo looks good in a notebook and bad in production. Where do you look?
pages.summary: I compare the string that was embedded, the filter, the packed ids, and the citation check. Most “model got worse” stories are one of those four.

pages.title: 4. How do you keep a knowledge bot from leaking across customers?
pages.summary: The filter is a security control. Identity and tenant are predicates on the query, not hints in the prompt. If the predicate is missing, I do not search.

pages.title: 5. When would you not use a vector index?
pages.summary: When the corpus is small enough to put in the prompt, when the question is an exact key lookup, or when you are not allowed to send the text to an embedding API and you have no local model approved.

pages.title: HNSW or IVFFlat?
pages.summary: HNSW for the README’s query trade if you can pay build time and memory, including on an empty table. IVFFlat when you have data and want the cheaper build, then measure.

pages.title: Where does the filter run?
pages.summary: After the approximate scan, unless you built a partial index or turned on iterative scans.

pages.title: What is k1?
pages.summary: BM25 term-frequency saturation. Elasticsearch’s default is 1.2.

pages.title: What is RRF?
pages.summary: A fusion of ranks. Elastic defaults the constant to 60. It does not read the document body.

pages.title: Name three vector databases and their limits.
pages.summary: I can name products. I will not invent caps. pgvector’s README numbers are the ones I can cite today.

pages.title: What does ef_search 40 imply for a selective filter?
pages.summary: The README’s example: if the condition matches 10% of rows and ef_search is the default 40, about 4 rows match. Filtering is after the scan unless you use a partial index or iterative scans.

pages.title: How do you size IVFFlat lists?
pages.summary: The README starts at rows/1000 up to 1M rows and sqrt(rows) above that. Create the index after the table has data, because there is a training step.

pages.title: What are Elastic’s RRF defaults?
pages.summary: rank_constant 60, at least 1. A higher constant gives lower ranks more influence. rank_window_size defaults to 10 and must be at least the requested size and at least 1.

pages.title: When do you use Hamming or Jaccard?
pages.summary: On bit vectors, as the README names those distances. They are not cosine on a float embedding.

pages.title: 1. What is an agent, and what is MCP?
pages.summary: An agent is a loop: the model requests a tool, my code runs it, the result comes back, and a budget stops us. MCP is a protocol — hosts, clients, servers, JSON-RPC — so that loop can discover tools, resources, and prompts from many servers. The protocol is not the loop, and the m

pages.title: 2. Walk a tool call on a phone call.
pages.summary: Speech becomes text. The model requests `transfer_to_queue` with a real queue id. The host speaks a confirmation. Only then do I call the tool, once, idempotently. The platform performs the transfer. The model does not own SIP.

pages.title: 3. How do you keep a tool-using bot from being a confused deputy?
pages.summary: I allow-list servers, I show the action before it runs, I ignore instructions that arrive inside tool descriptions, and I keep secrets out of the model’s arguments.

pages.title: 4. Compare OpenAI and Anthropic tool calling.
pages.summary: Both: I define a schema, the model requests a call, I execute, I send the result back. They differ in JSON, in how you force a tool, and in which models want which API.

pages.title: 5. What do you log, and when do you stop?
pages.summary: I log the model id, the tool name, redacted arguments, the allow decision, the result status, and the protocol revision. I stop on success of a side effect, on a budget, or on a deny.

pages.title: 1. When do you use more than one agent?
pages.summary: When one loop fails a golden case for a reason a specialist would fix. I still keep one host and one tool owner.

pages.title: 2. Who executes?
pages.summary: The host. MCP revision 2025-11-25. A specialist that prints tool JSON has not posted a ledger line.

pages.title: 3. How do you stop a double refund?
pages.summary: One agent holds the tool. The host runs it once. A reviewer does not get a copy “to verify.”

pages.title: 4. What is a multi-agent model id?
pages.summary: A string on a vendor page. xAI lists grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309. I pin it if I call it. I do not skip the host because the name sounds like this room.

pages.title: 5. How does this sit on a contact-center bot?
pages.summary: The caller hears one voice. The ledger has one writer. I will not convene a panel before the first audio token.

pages.title: 1. Why not ship on a demo?
pages.summary: A demo is one sample. I ship when a pinned bundle passes cases whose rules were written first, or a named owner waives a miss that is not a side effect.

pages.title: 2. How do you use an LLM as a judge without lying to yourself?
pages.summary: I give it a rubric and the evidence, I store its label separately, and I do not let it be the only gate on money. I overlap it with a human.

pages.title: 3. What is on the trace, and what is not?
pages.summary: Model id, prompt hash, retrieved ids, tool name, redacted arguments, allow or deny. Not a card number, and not a chain-of-thought treated as proof.

pages.title: 4. How do you watch production without turning customers into a test set?
pages.summary: I sample a rate I can name, I strip secrets, I score with the offline rules, and I keep the golden set. I do not hoard audio because a chart looks empty.

pages.title: 5. Design the gate for a contact-center bot in one pass.
pages.summary: Cases for answer, abstain, injection, double tool, and barge-in during consent. Deterministic graders. A waiver with a name and an expiry. Hold on unbounded money.

pages.title: 1. How do you trace a model call without worshipping a vendor?
pages.summary: I pin a conventions commit, I emit an operation name from that tree, and I keep a counter that does not depend on the trace vendor being up.

pages.title: 2. How do you build a cost budget without lying?
pages.summary: I date the pricing page, I pick the row that matches the model and the context length, and I multiply by calls including retries. I re-fetch before I forecast.

pages.title: 3. What is a latency budget if you refuse a universal millisecond number?
pages.summary: A list of hops I measure, compared with my own baseline. I page when a named hop regresses. I do not publish a single voice-latency SLO I have not timed on the real edge.

pages.title: 4. What is a guardrail you can implement this week without a new SKU?
pages.summary: A max input, a max number of tool rounds, an allow-list of tools, and a host check before any side effect. I count the denies.

pages.title: 1. How do you separate offline evals from checks in production?
pages.summary: I keep a file of named rows with pass rules, and I run it before deploy and again on a schedule. I also read a sample of live traces. I do not call unlabeled traffic a pass rate.

pages.title: 2. When is an LLM judge allowed to gate a release?
pages.summary: Almost never for money. A judge is a sample with known biases. A rule gates a refund, a cap, and a tool allow.

pages.title: 3. What do you mean by red teaming, and what do you still write by hand?
pages.summary: I mean generating test cases with another model, then having a person decide which failures block the build. I still hand-write the money cases.

pages.title: 4. How does prompt injection arrive through a tool or through MCP?
pages.summary: The tool result is text on the next turn. The host checks the second request. Annotations do not raise the cap. A human can deny.

pages.title: 5. What do you monitor, and what do you refuse to call quality?
pages.summary: I page on a failed named row, a deny count that drops to zero, and an unexpected tool span. I treat slow_down as a ramp. I do not page on a judge average over unlabeled traces.

pages.title: 1. When do you refuse to fine-tune?
pages.summary: When a prompt, a retriever, or a tool already fixes the failure, or when the train file is last month’s wrong promises. I measure that before I touch a rank.

pages.title: 2. Explain LoRA and QLoRA without a whiteboard of Greek.
pages.summary: LoRA trains a small update and leaves the original weights alone. QLoRA does that on a 4-bit frozen base so the base fits. Both still need an eval. Neither one is a license.

pages.title: 3. How do distillation and DPO differ?
pages.summary: Distillation copies a teacher into a smaller student. DPO fits a preference ranking with a classification loss and, in the paper, skips the RL loop. I do not mix the files.

pages.title: 4. A fine-tune was poisoned. What do you show an auditor?
pages.summary: The data hash, the case that should have flipped, and the tool that still enforces the cap. OWASP LLM04 names fine-tuning data as a poisoning surface. The adapter is not the control.

pages.title: 1. Draw a voice bot without stealing the ACD’s job.
pages.summary: The queue, the recording decision, and the transfer stay in CUCM, Webex, UCCE, or the CCaaS. ASR or a speech model, the decision, and TTS are treatments. I will not invent the admin clicks.

pages.title: 2. Explain barge-in.
pages.summary: The caller talks over playback. I stop the speaker immediately, cancel generation, and truncate the model’s audio to what was actually played. I do not run a tool on the overlap.

pages.title: 3. How do you talk about latency without a fake SLA?
pages.summary: I add hops: network, endpoint, ASR, model, tools, TTS, barge-in reaction. I cite the VAD sample’s 300 and 500 as examples. Every other number is a measurement I have or a TODO.

pages.title: 4. Containment, resolution, and the handoff.
pages.summary: Containment means no human. Resolution means the problem stayed fixed. The handoff packet tells the human what was already checked and what was promised. The model does not improvise that packet.

pages.title: 5. A latency spike on a Tuesday. Walk it.
pages.summary: I split the budget. If ASR is flat and tools grew, I cut tools. If the finish reason is the output cap, I fix the cap. I do not disable barge-in, and I do not treat the VAD sample as the culprit by default.

pages.title: Assist or virtual agent?
pages.summary: Virtual agent speaks to the customer. Assist speaks to the human. Actions are tools.

pages.title: Name a Webex bridge.
pages.summary: AI Agent Studio agents on voice and digital for the three product lines in the help article, plus the channels Webex Connect lists.

pages.title: Name a Connect bridge.
pages.summary: Customer AI agents for self-service and real-time assistance. Q in Connect on Bedrock, evolved from Wisdom, with the type enum.

pages.title: Google?
pages.summary: The CCAI connector Cisco documents, and the Agent Answers applicability sentence.

pages.title: Microsoft?
pages.summary: Teams is on the Webex connector list. Dynamics Copilot is the help pane plus autonomous handoff, from the Learn pages, with article paths dated and not walked on the lab tenant.

pages.title: What does autonomous mean on the Webex article?
pages.summary: A studio task the page names beside scripted agents. It is not permission to call every tool the tenant owns. The platform still owns the route.

pages.title: Does Agent Answers apply to Webex Contact Center?
pages.summary: The CCAI article says Agent Answers is not applicable to the Webex Contact Center solution. Do not sell it there on the strength of a different product’s sentence.

pages.title: What is an action on the Connect assistance list?
pages.summary: The page lists intent, generative responses, links, and actions. An action that moves money is a tool. The workspace button is not the post. The host or the configured flow posts.

pages.title: Where does a summary sit?
pages.summary: After the contact, as a draft the human reviews. Webex names reason, actions, resolution, and follow-ups, with a 24-hour API window after wrap-up.

pages.title: Virtual agent versus assist versus QM?
pages.summary: The customer, the human on the call, and a supervisor later. Three listeners. One host for tools.

pages.title: Name a workforce number you will defend.
pages.summary: Connect: 18 weeks scheduling, 64 weeks capacity, intraday every 15 minutes only at or above 5000 unique contacts per week per queue-channel.

pages.title: What must a quality score never decide?
pages.summary: Pay, seniority, or other employment rights. Dynamics prints that. Coaching is the use the page describes.

pages.title: Google bridge?
pages.summary: CCAI Platform Agent Assist: live help, wrap-up summaries per segment, and accuracy, completeness, adherence for the summary itself.

pages.title: How long can a dropped Webex call take to summarize?
pages.summary: Up to 60 seconds. A customer can call back before that processing finishes. Do not invent a faster guarantee.

pages.title: When does Webex allow a mid-call summary?
pages.summary: Direct agent-to-agent consults and transfers. Not transfers or consults routed to queues, entry points, dial numbers, or organisation contacts.

pages.title: Who sees a Connect generative summary, and where?
pages.summary: Agents: voice and email on the CCP for After Contact Work. Managers and supervisors: voice, chat, and email on the admin website. Do not swap the lists.

pages.title: What is Connect forecasting allowed to be in this room?
pages.summary: The starting point for scheduling and capacity planning. Short-term scheduling up to 18 weeks. Long-term capacity up to 64 weeks. It is the only WFM this room fetched.

pages.title: 2. Walk NIST’s core without a poster.
pages.summary: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage. Voluntary, 26 January 2023, being revised. Not a checklist. Measure is before launch, not after the outage.

pages.title: 3. What is excessive agency?
pages.summary: LLM06. The model can cause a side effect it should not. The fix is a short allow-list and a human on the exception, not a more careful adjective in the prompt.

pages.title: 4. How do you handle secrets and logs?
pages.summary: The system prompt is not a vault. I keep keys out of it, and I redact the prompt and payment data in the trace.

pages.title: 1. Where does a card number leak in a voice bot?
pages.summary: Audio, transcript, DTMF, tool arguments, the summary a human will read aloud, the trace, the eval file, and the fine-tune. I design the sinks first.

pages.title: 2. How do you implement consent without trusting the model?
pages.summary: I log an event: prompt completed, interrupted, or absent. The tool requires completed. A JSON boolean from the model does not count.

pages.title: 3. Someone says recordings are deleted after 30 minutes. What do you answer?
pages.summary: I ask which page. The Dynamics article I fetched says the conversation closes after 30 minutes of inactivity if it was not escalated. Close is not delete.

pages.title: 4. How do you test redaction?
pages.summary: I send a known fake sensitive token through every sink and I read the log. A toggle I did not test is not a control. NIST Measure is before deployment and again in operation.

pages.title: 1. Design a voice agent for a contact center. You have the board.
pages.summary: A read-only bot answers from one index, abstains or transfers when the pack misses, and a kill switch returns the call to humans. No refund tool in the first release.

pages.title: 2. What is the eval plan?
pages.summary: Recall, faithfulness, trajectory, and a redaction check. Injection is a case, not a footnote. A judge does not gate it.

pages.title: 3. How do you roll it out?
pages.summary: Shadow on synthetic traffic, then one queue I can drain, then wider only with my own hop measurements. The kill switch is practiced.

pages.title: 4. What do you refuse to invent when they push for a number?
pages.summary: A universal millisecond SLO, a word-error rate, a PCI scope, a retention period, and a dial-plan id. I can compute a token cost from a dated price row.
